newsitem.title: UK: Japanese stocks in London up slightly, trade thin.
newsitem.headline: Japanese stocks in London up slightly, trade thin.

text.p: Japanese shares in Europe were marginally higher in thin trade on Tuesday, underpinned by selective buying in banking issues, dealers said.
But trading volumes remained light as European investors worried about Wall Street's volatility.
"It has been very quiet. But we have seen a few buyers in the banks," one dealer said. "Some people think Tokyo will come to the rescue of the banks and their bad loans."
In Tokyo on Tuesday, the Nikkei-225 share index closed 391.70 points higher at 18,445.20 as market participants applauded government plans to boost the stagnant land market.

Japanese banks, which are heavily exposed to land developers, benefited from comments from finance minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka who told a news conference in Tokyo on Tuesday that the government would introduce measures to improve land liquidity by March 31.
Sanwa Bank 8320Q.L was trading at 1,362.5 yen by 1515 GMT versus a Tokyo close of 1,360 yen.
